plan.because: The supplied contract identifies the parties, property and tenancy terms.
Obtain the report to the landlord establishing which defects were reported and when.
Establish whether and when the landlord received the defect report.
Document the visible defects, locations and observation dates.
Establish the response, proposed work and access arrangements.
Mould or moisture is raised but remains uncertain; applicability depends on clarification.
Heating is not mentioned and is presumed absent for planning.
Health effects are reported; obtain the findings and any limits on attributed cause.
A need for specialist inspection is not mentioned and is presumed absent for planning; the electrical safety risk still needs urgent attention.
A rent deposit is contemplated; establish any deadline communicated to the landlord and its contents.
This document is optional under the process.

questions: For immediate electrical safety, avoid using the affected sockets and appliances and seek urgent assistance from an electrician or the emergency services if danger is immediate. Is there a current sparking, fire or shock risk?
When and how did you notify the landlord of each defect, and can you provide the reports and delivery evidence?
Have you communicated a written repair deadline to the landlord? If so, when and for what date?
Are the hallway spots mould or is the wall damp? Have they been inspected or measured?
What responses or access arrangements, if any, has the landlord proposed?
